pairs.rationale: Two accounts of the same event, possibly different documents.
Wang discusses a dream allusion, supplies two versions and gives no sound preference.
Documentary correction from recollection to the epitaph.
Sources assign different forms and genres. No direct sound comparison.
Gong explicitly prefers 寸 for correspondence to 眾.
Witnesses reverse 意 and 自. Xie discusses diction.
Economy praised over unquoted drafts; the two extant versions both represent Wang's solution.

Li as reported by Sun favours his own opening on the same set topic. Another account discusses the auspicious sun shining by night. Neither specifies a sound preference. Hao's first two graphs follow Sun.
Chen reports Teng conceding precedence. Both examples in this witness use 圜, where Sun prints 圓. No explicit sound rationale.
Zhang Dun as reported by Wang favours the longer ending for cadence. Known since Stage 1. The shorter tails are inserted into the same received context.
Xie explicitly records a rewrite of these two tails. Only the attested tails are juxtaposed for measurement. He gives no reason or preference.
Wang supplies a two-character alternative in a parenthesis. Praise concerns the document as a whole.
Collected text supplies a third attested wording and connective. No directional judgment.

reading_notes: Controlled Standard Mandarin citation targets. 見夢 uses xian4 ‘appear in a dream’; jian4 remains possible as a reading of 見. 不勝 uses contemporary sheng4; literary sheng1 also occurs. 傅說 fu4 yue4, 單于 chan2 yu2, 賁 bi4 (adorn), and musical 樂 yue4 are context selections. Preserve source graphs including 歳 and 曵. Punctuation is editorial and standardized within pairs. Source tables distinguish diplomatic readings from performance text. Familiar equivalents such as 袞/衮, 羹/羮 and 眾/衆 are normalized for some versions. No spelling difference is counted as a reported aesthetic preference.
